mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two months compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for four months compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their respective 6-month averages indicates a simultaneous expansion in employment and a decline in unemployment, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed 6-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 6-month averages compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) above its 3-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening household purchasing power, which drives higher consumer spending and corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS exceeds 3-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods when RSAFS is above its 3-month moving average for five months compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
